subject: Acme private deployment: demarcation, control-plane/data-plane, and runbook review
messages:
From: Sam Tan <sam.tan@acme-robotics.com>
To: aisha_rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
Cc: pm-ops@acme-robotics.com
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: review of private VPC demarcation + control/data-plane split

Hi Aisha,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We're finalizing our network perimeter for the private deployment and want to validate the control-plane/data-plane boundaries you recommended. Attached is our current demarcation diagram and a rough deploy runbook.

High level asks:
- Confirm control-plane endpoints we should allow over the customer VPC (port/host expectations).
- Verify recommended egress pattern for model telemetry and health-check pings (we'd like to avoid broad 0.0.0.0 egress rules).
- Feedback on an ops-friendly handoff runbook we can use for cutover (we plan staged cutovers per region).

Can you review and propose any changes? If useful, we can schedule a short sync with your infra team (Monica / Vivek).

Attachments: acme-vpc-demarc-v1.pdf, runbook-deploy-steps.md

Thanks,
Sam Tan
Head of Platform Operations
Acme Robotics
From: aisha_rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Tan <sam.tan@acme-robotics.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: review of private VPC demarcation + control/data-plane split

Hi Sam — thanks for sending these over. Monica and Vivek are looped in; they're owners for network and deployment runbook respectively. We'll take a pass and put inline comments into the diagram PDF, plus a short revised runbook.

Quick answers up front so you have time to plan:
- Control-plane: expect a small number of outbound HTTPS endpoints from control-plane agents to the Redwood control plane (api.redwood.ai and auth.redwood.ai). We recommend allowing outbound to a narrow set of FQDNs/IP ranges rather than wildcard egress. We'll provide the precise CIDR list and FQDNs in our follow-up.
- Data-plane: model-serving nodes should not initiate control-plane management traffic. Management/control connections originate from the control-plane bastion into the data-plane over mTLS on specific management ports (we'll call out the ports in the next note).
- Telemetry: prefer a push model from an ops aggregator inside the VPC to push to telemetry.redwood.ai over an outbound TLS tunnel; avoid opening broad egress from every model node.

Can we schedule a 30 min sync tomorrow at 10:00am PT to walk the diagrams and confirm the runbook cutover steps? If that works, we'll share a draft meeting agenda and the annotated diagrams.

Cheers,
Aisha Rahman
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>

Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2027 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Request: review of private VPC demarcation + control/data-plane split

Hi Sam — Monica here (networking). Took a look at the PDF; a couple of immediate suggestions before our call:

- Recommend isolating control-plane management traffic into a dedicated subnet with security groups that only permit outbound TLS to the Redwood control-plane IP set. We'll provide a /28 suggestion for the management subnet so it's small and auditable.
- For health checks: prefer a single outbound LB/egress proxy that performs TLS termination and forwards to telemetry.redwood.ai; this avoids needing the control-plane to hold many egress rules.
- Port list: management (mTLS) 8443, metrics/health 9411 (prom metrics push), agent heartbeat 5222 (if you keep the XMPP-style heartbeat). We'll confirm exact ports in the follow up doc.

I've attached a lightweight drawio with inline callouts for where to place the proxy and the management subnet. Vivek, can you take the runbook and add the cutover rollback checklist (database snapshots, model cache invalidation, traffic-shift steps)?

Thanks,
Monica
Network Lead, Redwood Inference
Attachments: controlplane-dataflow.drawio

Date: Wed, 24 Mar 2027 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Request: review of private VPC demarcation + control/data-plane split

Thanks everyone — good call today. Quick status and next artifacts we uploaded:

- Uploaded: acme-vpc-demarc-v2.pdf (annotated with control-plane CIDRs and the management /28), controlplane-dataflow.drawio (with proxy placement), runbook-deploy-steps.md (added rollback checklist and traffic-shift steps). Drive links below.
- Action items for Acme before cutover: 1) Provision the management subnet /28 and security groups per the annotated PDF, 2) Stand up the egress proxy with TLS termination + firewall rules, 3) Confirm the CIDR allowlist at least 48 hours before cutover for our testing window.
- Telemetry: we'll hand over a bootstrap script to configure the aggregator VM and the cert rotation schedule.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1A2b3Cacme-vpc-demarc
Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/ACME+Private+Deploy+Runbook

If there are no outstanding questions, we can target the staged cutover week of Apr 12th (region us-west-2 first). I'll file the runbook into the shared runbook folder and tag the oncall rotation.

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
Platform Engineering Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachments: acme-vpc-demarc-v2.pdf, controlplane-dataflow.drawio, runbook-deploy-steps.md
